status: development diagnostic; stimuli inspected; not preregistered or held out
selection_reason: All items in two previously selected suites test number dependencies across a PP distractor. Selection is independent of parser success; no source sentences are rewritten.
task: Derived whole-sentence licensing contrast: match_sing and match_plural should be accepted; mismatch_sing and mismatch_plural should be rejected.
original_task: Regional surprisal inequalities. These remain preserved and unscored: the grammar engines supply no normalized word probabilities.
family_unit: One suite/item has four conditions. The same item number in both selected suites shares a lexical frame and must stay in one split.
split: All 19 shared lexical frames are development material. Lexicon declarations use both suites. No held-out generalization estimate, significance test or independent-family confidence interval.
primary_measure: All four conditions correct in an evaluable family; ties or accept-all do not pass a family.
negative_credit: Only an explicit feature conflict on an otherwise complete derivation counts as rejection in the new constraint engines. Failure to derive in an unextended engine is unavailable, never negative credit.

component_contrasts.head_vs_none: Same diagnostic CCG lexicon and application rules; enable subject-number and local reflexive-number constraints.
component_contrasts.head_vs_nearest: Keep constraints and lexicon; change controller from the subject NP head to its last nominal.

interpretation_limits: A deliberately narrow CCG plus typed-feature hybrid, not a full HPSG or binding theory.
Gender is not tested; singular masculine reflexives assume a context permitting a masculine referent.
No calibrated surprisal, reading-time fit, learned neural model, new human data or claim of superiority over DS.
A correct result on source-informed development examples verifies implementation of the stated dependency, not discovery of that dependency.
